SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Milk souring
   D. Paper burning to ash

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.

6. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Producers
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. newton (N)

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

12. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

13. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

14. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
